# std.http; connection/application state stays inside its actor heap.

# Application messages use the same bounded, copied actor delivery as std.actor.
pub enum Notice[M]:
    Message(M)
    Drain
    Resume
    Completed
    Rejected

    Body(Bytes)

# Only owned bytes and scalars survive a callback; heads are encoded before
# they enter this queue. Partial writes resume without retaining a borrow.
pub class Response:
    _output: Bytes
    _start: i64
    _limit: i64
    _state: i64
    _remaining: i64
    _head: bool
    _minor: i64
    _keep: bool
    _stopping: bool
    _body_done: bool
    _shutdown: bool

    pub def is_stopping(self) -> bool:
        self._stopping

    pub def close_after(self: &mut Response) -> ():
        self._keep = False

    # Request server shutdown after this response, without a shared token in
    # the connection heap. Admission receives an ordinary copied message.
    pub def shutdown_server(self: &mut Response) -> ():
        self._shutdown = True
        self._keep = False

    pub def is_started(self) -> bool:
        self._state != 0

    pub def is_done(self) -> bool:
        self._state == 4

    pub def pending(self) -> i64:
        self._output.len() - self._start

    pub def space(self) -> i64:
        mut room = self._limit - self.pending() - 64
        if room < 0:
            room = 0
        room

    def begin_response(self: &mut Response, head: ResponseHead, reserve: i64) -> Result[(), HttpError | BytesError | AllocError]:
        if self._state != 0:
            return Err(HttpError.Broken)
        mut owned = head
        if owned.status < 200:
            return Err(HttpError.InvalidStatusLine)
        if std.http.find(&owned.headers, "transfer-encoding").is_some():
            return Err(HttpError.ConflictingFraming)
        if owned.status == 204 and std.http.find(&owned.headers, "content-length").is_some():
            return Err(HttpError.ConflictingFraming)
        # Use HTTP/1.1 persistence here to test the application's close token;
        # request persistence and the emitted version are handled separately.
        owned.minor = 1
        if not std.http.response_keeps_alive(&owned, &Framing.Length(0)):
            self._keep = False
        mut state = 1
        mut length = 0
        match std.http.response_framing(&owned, "GET")?:
            case Framing.Length(size):
                length = size
            case Framing.Empty:
                pass
            case _:
                if self._minor == 1:
                    state = 2
                    owned.add("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")?
                else:
                    state = 3
                    self._keep = False
        owned.minor = self._minor
        if not self._body_done or self._stopping:
            self._keep = False
        if not self._keep:
            owned.add("Connection", "close")?
        elif self._minor == 0:
            owned.add("Connection", "keep-alive")?
        encoded = std.http.encode_response(&owned)?
        if encoded.len() > self._limit - self.pending() - 64:
            return Err(HttpError.HeadTooLarge)
        if reserve > self._limit - self.pending() - 64 - encoded.len():
            return Err(HttpError.BodyTooLarge)
        self.compact()?
        self._output.extend(&encoded)?
        self._state = state
        self._remaining = length
        Ok(())

    # A short result is back-pressure. Keep the remainder and resume on
    # Writable; this never waits for a socket and never exceeds the queue.
    def _write[S: ByteSource](self: &mut Response, source: &S, start: i64, stop: i64) -> Result[i64, HttpError | BytesError]:
        if self._state < 1 or self._state > 3:
            return Err(HttpError.Broken)
        if start < 0 or stop < start or stop > source.len():
            return Err(BytesError.OutOfRange)
        if self._state == 1 and stop - start > self._remaining and not self._head:
            return Err(HttpError.LengthMismatch)
        if self._head:
            return Ok(stop - start)
        mut count = stop - start
        if count > self.space():
            count = self.space()
        if count == 0:
            return Ok(0)
        self.compact()?
        if self._state == 2:
            size = std.http.encode_chunk_size(count)?
            self._output.extend(&size)?
        self._output.extend_range(source, start, start + count)?
        if self._state == 2:
            self._output.extend(b"\r\n")?
        elif self._state == 1:
            self._remaining -= count
        Ok(count)

    def _finish(self: &mut Response) -> Result[(), HttpError | BytesError]:
        if self._state < 1 or self._state > 3:
            return Err(HttpError.Broken)
        if self._state == 1 and self._remaining != 0 and not self._head:
            return Err(HttpError.LengthMismatch)
        if self._state == 2 and not self._head:
            self.compact()?
            self._output.extend(b"0\r\n\r\n")?
        self._state = 4
        Ok(())

    def _respond[S: ByteSource](self: &mut Response, head: ResponseHead, body: &S) -> Result[(), HttpError | BytesError | AllocError]:
        mut owned = head
        if std.http.find(&owned.headers, "content-length").is_some() or std.http.find(&owned.headers, "transfer-encoding").is_some():
            return Err(HttpError.ConflictingFraming)
        if (owned.status == 204 or owned.status == 304) and body.len() != 0:
            return Err(HttpError.LengthMismatch)
        if body.len() > self.space() and not self._head:
            return Err(HttpError.BodyTooLarge)
        if owned.status != 204 and owned.status != 304:
            owned.add("Content-Length", str.from(body.len())?)?
        self.begin_response(owned, 0 if self._head else body.len())?
        if self._write(body, 0, body.len())? != body.len():
            return Err(HttpError.BodyTooLarge)
        self._finish()?
        Ok(())

    def _send[S: ByteSource](self: &mut Response, status: i64, content_type: &str, body: &S) -> Result[(), HttpError | BytesError | AllocError]:
        mut head = std.http.response(status, std.http.server.reason(status))?
        head.add("Content-Type", *content_type)?
        self._respond(head, body)

    def _send_text(self: &mut Response, status: i64, text: &str) -> Result[(), HttpError | BytesError | AllocError]:
        self._send(status, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", &std.bytes.from_text(text)?)

    def compact(self: &mut Response) -> Result[(), BytesError]:
        if self._start > 0:
            self._output.copy_within(self._start, self._output.len(), 0)?
            self._output.truncate(self.pending())?
            self._start = 0
        Ok(())

    pub def start(self: &mut Response, head: ResponseHead) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        network(self.begin_response(head, 0))

    pub def write[S: ByteSource](self: &mut Response, source: &S, start: i64, stop: i64) -> Result[i64, ServerError]:
        network(self._write(source, start, stop))

    pub def finish(self: &mut Response) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        network(self._finish())

    pub def respond[S: ByteSource](self: &mut Response, head: ResponseHead, body: &S) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        network(self._respond(head, body))

    pub def send[S: ByteSource](self: &mut Response, status: i64, content_type: &str, body: &S) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        network(self._send(status, content_type, body))

    pub def send_text(self: &mut Response, status: i64, text: &str) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        network(self._send_text(status, text))

pub def config() -> Config:

# The same driver uses TCP or TLS. Both transports advance only on available

enum Wire:
    Plain(Connection)
    Secure(TlsConnection)

    pub def input(self) -> &Bytes:

    pub def input_start(self) -> i64:
        match self:
            case Wire.Plain(connection):
                connection.input_start()
            case Wire.Secure(connection):
                connection.input_start()

    pub def input_stop(self) -> i64:
        match self:
            case Wire.Plain(connection):
                connection.input_stop()
            case Wire.Secure(connection):
                connection.input_stop()

    pub def available(self) -> i64:
        match self:
            case Wire.Plain(connection):
                connection.available()
            case Wire.Secure(connection):
                connection.available()

    pub def pending(self) -> i64:
        match self:
            case Wire.Plain(connection):

            case Wire.Secure(connection):
                connection.pending()

    pub def reading(self) -> bool:

            case Wire.Secure(connection):

            case Wire.Secure(connection):

    pub def handle[M](self: &mut Wire, mail: &Mail[Notice[M], ServerError], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[std.actor.net.Events, ServerError]:

            case Wire.Plain(connection):
                network(connection.handle(mail, context))
            case Wire.Secure(connection):

    pub def consume[M](self: &mut Wire, count: i64, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:

            case Wire.Plain(connection):
                network(connection.consume(count, context))
            case Wire.Secure(connection):
                network(connection.consume(count, context))

    pub def write[M](self: &mut Wire, bytes: &Bytes, start: i64, stop: i64, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[i64, ServerError]:

            case Wire.Plain(connection):
                network(connection.write(bytes, start, stop, context))
            case Wire.Secure(connection):
                network(connection.write(bytes, start, stop, context))

    pub def shutdown_write[M](self: &mut Wire, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match self:
            case Wire.Plain(connection):
                network(connection.shutdown_write(context))
            case Wire.Secure(connection):
                network(connection.shutdown_write(context))

    pub def close[M](self: &mut Wire, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match self:
            case Wire.Plain(connection):
                network(connection.close(context))
            case Wire.Secure(connection):
                network(connection.close(context))

    pub def read_within[M](self: &mut Wire, span: &Duration, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match self:
            case Wire.Plain(connection):
                network(connection.read_within(span, context))
            case Wire.Secure(connection):
                network(connection.read_within(span, context))

def network[T, E](result: Result[T, E]) -> Result[T, ServerError]:
    match result:
        case Ok(value):
            Ok(value)
        case Err(error):
            Err(server_error(error))

def storage[T, E](result: Result[T, E]) -> Result[T, ServerError]:
    match result:
        case Ok(value):
            Ok(value)
        case Err(error):
            Err(server_error(error))

class Acceptor[F]:
    socket: TcpListener
    factory: F
    config: Config
    tls: Option[ServerConfig]
    children: Option[list[Address]]
    watch: Option[Watch]
    address: Option[Address]
    draining: bool
    requests: u64
    rejected: u64
    protocol_errors: u64


    def receive[M](self: &mut Acceptor[F], mail: Mail[Notice[M], ServerError], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match mail:
            case Mail.Ready(watch, _):
                if not self.draining and self.watch.unwrap().key() == watch.key():
                    match &mut self.children:
                        case Some(children):
                            if len(children) < self.config.capacity:
                                match context.spawn_isolated(0, self.config.heap_limit):
                                    case Ok(child):
                                        storage(children.append(child))?
                                        return Ok(())
                                    case Err(_):
                                        pass
                        case Nothing:
                            pass
                    # Refusing never blocks or constructs TLS state.
                    drop(self.socket.accept_now())
                    self.rejected += 1u64
            case Mail.Down(child, _, _):
                match &mut self.children:
                    case Some(children):
                        for index in range(len(children)):
                            if children[index].key() == child.key():
                                last = children.pop().unwrap()
                                if index < len(children):
                                    children[index] = last
                                break
                    case Nothing:
                        pass
            case Mail.Message(Notice.Completed):
                self.requests += 1u64
            case Mail.Message(Notice.Rejected):
                self.protocol_errors += 1u64
            case Mail.Message(Notice.Drain):
                if not self.draining:
                    self.draining = True
                    drop(context.unwatch(&self.socket))
                    drop(self.socket.close())
                # Retrying Drain is intentional: bounded child mailboxes may
                # have been full during an earlier notification.
                match &self.children:
                    case Some(children):
                        for child in children:
                            drop(context.send(*child, Notice[M].Drain))
                    case Nothing:
                        pass
            case _:
                pass
        Ok(())

    def done(self) -> bool:
        if not self.draining:
            return False
        match &self.children:
            case Some(children):
                len(children) == 0
            case Nothing:
                True

class Client[F, H]:
    socket: Option[TcpStream]
    factory: F
    config: Config
    session: Option[Session]
    parent: Address
    handler: Option[H]
    wire: Option[Wire]
    decoder: Option[Decoder]
    response: Option[Response]
    requests: i64
    phase: i64
    timer: Option[Timer]
    draining: bool
    lingering: i64
    reported: bool
    resuming: bool
    completing: bool
    shutdown_pending: bool
    retiring: bool
    failure: Option[ServerError]


    def set_deadline[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match replace(self.timer, Nothing):
            case Some(timer):
                drop(context.cancel(timer))
            case Nothing:
                pass
        span = match self.phase:
            case 0:
                nanoseconds(self.config.handshake_timeout.as_nanoseconds())
            case 1:
                nanoseconds(self.config.idle_timeout.as_nanoseconds())
            case 2:
                nanoseconds(self.config.head_timeout.as_nanoseconds())
            case 3:
                nanoseconds(self.config.body_timeout.as_nanoseconds())
            case 5:
                seconds(2u32)
            case _:
                nanoseconds(self.config.response_timeout.as_nanoseconds())
        if span.as_nanoseconds() > 0u64:
            self.timer = Some(network(context.after(&span, -1))?)
        Ok(())

    def resume[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        if not self.resuming:
            # A bounded continuation yields without a timer. A full mailbox
            # already makes this actor runnable, so it needs no extra wakeup.
            match context.send(context.address(), Notice[M].Resume):
                case Ok(_):
                    self.resuming = True
                case Err(_):
                    pass
        Ok(())

    def has_control(self) -> bool:
        self.shutdown_pending or self.completing

    def flush_control[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> ():
        if self.shutdown_pending:
            match context.send(self.parent, Notice[M].Drain):
                case Ok(_):
                    self.shutdown_pending = False
                case Err(_):
                    pass
        if self.completing:
            match context.send(self.parent, Notice[M].Completed):
                case Ok(_):
                    self.completing = False
                    self.reported = True
                case Err(_):
                    pass

    def stop[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        self.retiring = True
        if self.has_control():
            self.resume(context)?
        else:
            context.stop()
        Ok(())

    def receive[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], mail: Mail[Notice[M], ServerError], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match &mail:
            case Mail.Message(Notice.Resume):
                self.resuming = False
            case _:
                pass
        self.flush_control(context)
        if self.retiring:
            # The connection has already ended. Keep only its bounded control
            # notifications alive; application mail no longer has a recipient.
            if self.has_control():
                self.resume(context)?
                return Ok(())
            match replace(self.failure, Nothing):
                case Some(error):
                    return Err(error)
                case Nothing:
                    context.stop()
                    return Ok(())
        # A full parent mailbox never discards live application messages or
        # one-shot timers. Only final retirement waits for control delivery.
        match self.drive(mail, context):
            case Ok(_):
                Ok(())
            case Err(error):
                if not self.has_control():
                    return Err(error)
                self.retiring = True
                self.failure = Some(error)
                self.resume(context)?
                Ok(())

    def drive[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], mail: Mail[Notice[M], ServerError], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        mut wire = replace(self.wire, Nothing).unwrap()
        mut decoder = replace(self.decoder, Nothing).unwrap()
        mut reply = replace(self.response, Nothing).unwrap()
        mut handler = replace(self.handler, Nothing).unwrap()
        events = wire.handle(&mail, context)?
        if events.expired.is_some():
            wire.close(context)?
            self.stop(context)?
        else:
            match mail:
                case Mail.Timer(timer):
                    match &self.timer:
                        case Some(phase_timer):
                            if timer.key() == phase_timer.key():
                                if self.phase == 2 or self.phase == 3:
                                    self.refuse(&mut reply, 408)?
                                    self.phase = 4
                                    self.set_deadline(context)?
                                else:
                                    wire.close(context)?
                                    self.stop(context)?
                                    return Ok(())
                        case Nothing:
                            pass
                    if timer.tag() >= 0 and not events.mine:
                        self.call(&mut handler, Event[M].Actor(Mail[Notice[M], ServerError].Timer(timer)), &mut reply, context)?
                case Mail.Message(Notice.Resume):
                    self.resuming = False
                case Mail.Message(Notice.Message(message)):
                    self.call(&mut handler, Event[M].Message(message), &mut reply, context)?
                case Mail.Message(Notice.Drain):
                    if not self.draining:
                        self.draining = True
                        reply._stopping = True
                        reply._keep = False
                        if self.phase <= 1:
                            self.close_after_flush(&mut wire, context)?
                        else:
                            self.call(&mut handler, Event[M].Stopping, &mut reply, context)?
                case Mail.Ready(watch, ready):
                    if not events.mine:
                        self.call(&mut handler, Event[M].Actor(Mail[Notice[M], ServerError].Ready(watch, ready)), &mut reply, context)?
                case Mail.Stop:
                    drop(wire.close(context))
                    return Ok(())
                case _ as other:
                    self.call(&mut handler, Event[M].Actor(other), &mut reply, context)?
            if not self.retiring:
                self.advance(&mut wire, &mut decoder, &mut reply, &mut handler, context)?
        self.wire = Some(wire)
        self.decoder = Some(decoder)
        self.response = Some(reply)
        self.handler = Some(handler)
        Ok(())

    def call[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], handler: &mut H, event: Event[M], reply: &mut Response, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        outcome = handler.receive(event, reply, context)
        if reply._shutdown:
            self.shutdown_pending = True
            reply._shutdown = False
        self.flush_control(context)
        match outcome:
            case Ok(_):
                pass
            case Err(_):
                if reply.is_started():
                    return Err(ServerError.Handler)
                self.refuse(reply, 500)?
        Ok(())

    def refuse(self: &mut Client[F, H], reply: &mut Response, status: i64) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        if reply.is_started():
            return Err(ServerError.Http(HttpError.Broken))
        reply._keep = False
        reply._body_done = True
        network(reply.send_text(status, std.http.server.reason(status)))?
        self.phase = 4
        Ok(())

    def close_after_flush[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], wire: &mut Wire, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        wire.shutdown_write(context)?
        self.phase = 5
        self.set_deadline(context)?
        if not wire.reading() and wire.pending() == 0:
            self.stop(context)?
        else:
            self.resume(context)?
        Ok(())

    def advance[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], wire: &mut Wire, decoder: &mut Decoder, reply: &mut Response, handler: &mut H, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        if self.shutdown_pending:
            self.resume(context)?
            return Ok(())
        if self.phase == 0:
            if not wire.established():
                return Ok(())
            self.phase = 1
            self.set_deadline(context)?
        if self.phase == 5:
            count = wire.available()
            self.lingering += count
            wire.consume(count, context)?
            if (not wire.reading() or self.lingering >= 16777216) and wire.pending() == 0:
                wire.close(context)?
                self.stop(context)?
            elif wire.available() > 0:
                self.resume(context)?
            return Ok(())
        if self.phase == 1 and wire.available() > 0:
            self.phase = 2
            self.set_deadline(context)?
        # Bounded decoder events per actor turn. A continuation timer handles
        # input already buffered when no further socket readiness is needed.
        mut progress = False
        for _ in range(16):
            if self.phase != 2 and self.phase != 3:
                break
            if reply.is_started() and not reply.is_done() and reply.space() == 0:
                break
            next = decoder.feed(wire.input(), wire.input_start(), wire.input_stop())
            match next:
                case Err(error):
                    drop(context.send(self.parent, Notice[M].Rejected))
                    self.refuse(reply, error_status(&error))?
                    self.phase = 4
                    self.set_deadline(context)?
                    break
                case Ok(pair):
                    consumed, event = pair
                    wire.consume(consumed, context)?
                    progress = consumed > 0
                    match event:
                        case Some(std.http.decoder.Event.Head(head, target, framing)):
                            self.requests += 1
                            reply._head = head.method == "HEAD"
                            reply._minor = head.minor
                            reply._keep = not self.draining and self.requests < self.config.max_requests and std.http.request_keeps_alive(&head)
                            expect = wants_continue(&head)
                            self.phase = 3
                            self.set_deadline(context)?
                            self.call(handler, Event[M].Head(head, target), reply, context)?
                            if expect and not reply.is_started():
                                match framing:
                                    case Framing.Length(0) | Framing.Empty:
                                        pass
                                    case _:
                                        storage(reply._output.extend(b"HTTP/1.1 100 Continue\r\n\r\n"))?
                            progress = True
                        case Some(std.http.decoder.Event.Body(bytes)):
                            self.call(handler, Event[M].Body(bytes), reply, context)?
                            progress = True
                        case Some(std.http.decoder.Event.Trailers(fields)):
                            self.call(handler, Event[M].Trailers(fields), reply, context)?
                            progress = True
                        case Some(std.http.decoder.Event.End):
                            reply._body_done = True
                            self.phase = 4
                            self.set_deadline(context)?
                            self.call(handler, Event[M].End, reply, context)?
                            progress = True
                        case Nothing:
                            pass
                    if reply.is_done() and not reply._body_done:
                        reply._keep = False
                        self.phase = 4
                        self.set_deadline(context)?
                    if not progress:
                        break
        if not wire.reading() and wire.available() == 0 and not progress and (self.phase == 2 or self.phase == 3):
            match decoder.finish():
                case Err(error):
                    self.refuse(reply, error_status(&error))?
                    self.phase = 4
                case Ok(_):
                    self.close_after_flush(wire, context)?
                    return Ok(())
        if self.phase == 1 and not wire.reading():
            self.close_after_flush(wire, context)?
            return Ok(())
        if self.shutdown_pending:
            self.resume(context)?
            return Ok(())
        before = reply.pending()
        if before > 0:
            mut stop = reply._output.len()
            if stop - reply._start > 16384:
                stop = reply._start + 16384
            count = wire.write(&reply._output, reply._start, stop, context)?
            reply._start += count
            if reply._start == reply._output.len():
                reply._output.clear()
                reply._start = 0
            if count > 0 and not reply.is_done() and reply.is_started():
                self.call(handler, Event[M].Writable, reply, context)?
        if self.shutdown_pending:
            self.resume(context)?
            return Ok(())
        if reply.is_done() and reply.pending() == 0 and wire.pending() == 0:
            if not self.reported:
                match context.send(self.parent, Notice[M].Completed):
                    case Ok(_):
                        self.reported = True
                    case Err(_):
                        self.completing = True
                        self.resume(context)?
                        return Ok(())
            if not reply._keep or self.draining:
                self.close_after_flush(wire, context)?
                return Ok(())
            network(decoder.reset())?
            reply._state = 0
            reply._remaining = 0
            reply._body_done = False
            self.reported = False
            self.phase = 1
            self.set_deadline(context)?
            progress = wire.available() > 0
        if progress or (reply.pending() > 0 and wire.pending() == 0):
            self.resume(context)?
        Ok(())

# phase 0 handshake, 1 idle, 2 head, 3 body, 4 response, 5 lingering.
# Only one request is decoded at a time; pipelined input remains in the
# bounded transport buffer until its preceding response has drained.
enum State[F, H]:
    Accepting(Acceptor[F])
    Serving(Client[F, H])

# Public for cross-module generic Stage dispatch; construction stays private.
pub class Node[F, H]:
    _state: State[F, H]

    pub def started[M](self: &mut Node[F, H], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match &mut self._state:
            case State.Accepting(acceptor):
                acceptor.address = Some(context.address())
                acceptor.children = Some(storage(list[Address].with_capacity(acceptor.config.capacity))?)
                acceptor.watch = Some(network(context.watch(&acceptor.socket, Interest.Read))?)
            case State.Serving(client):
                mut socket = match replace(client.socket, Nothing):
                    case Some(stream):
                        stream
                    case Nothing:
                        context.stop()
                        return Ok(())
                drop(socket.set_no_delay(True))
                limits = std.actor.net.Limits(client.config.input_buffer, client.config.output_buffer, seconds(0u32), nanoseconds(client.config.write_timeout.as_nanoseconds()))
                net = network(std.actor.net.connection(socket, &limits))?
                mut wire = match replace(client.session, Nothing):
                    case Some(session):
                        Wire.Secure(network(std.actor.tls.over(net, session, client.config.input_buffer))?)
                    case Nothing:
                        Wire.Plain(net)
                wire.start(context)?
                client.phase = 0 if not wire.established() else 1
                client.wire = Some(wire)
                client.handler = Some(application(client.factory.create())?)
                client.decoder = Some(storage(std.http.decoder.decoder(&client.config.limits))?)
                client.response = Some(storage(response(client.config.pending_output))?)
                client.set_deadline(context)?
        Ok(())

    pub def receive[M](self: &mut Node[F, H], mail: Mail[Notice[M], ServerError], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match &mut self._state:
            case State.Accepting(acceptor):
                acceptor.receive(mail, context)
            case State.Serving(client):
                client.receive(mail, context)

    pub def spawn[M](self, tag: i64, child: Address, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[Option[Node[F, H]], ServerError]:
        match &self._state:
            case State.Accepting(acceptor):
                stream: Option[TcpStream] = match acceptor.socket.accept_now():
                    case Ok(socket):
                        Some(socket)
                    case Err(_):
                        Nothing
                session: Option[Session] = match &acceptor.tls:
                    case Some(tls):
                        Some(network(server_session(tls))?)
                    case Nothing:
                        Nothing
                # TLS configs cannot be copied. The session is constructed in
                # the child heap under isolated admission; any failure retires
                # this child. User factory and socket buffers run in started.
                Ok(Some(Node[F, H](State[F, H].Serving(Client[F, H](stream, storage(copy(&acceptor.factory))?, storage(copy(&acceptor.config))?, session, acceptor.address.unwrap(), Nothing, Nothing, Nothing, Nothing, 0, 1, Nothing, False, 0, False, False, False, False, False, Nothing)))))
            case State.Serving(_):
                Ok(Nothing)

def error_status(error: &HttpError) -> i64:
    match error:
        case HttpError.LineTooLong | HttpError.HeadTooLarge | HttpError.TooManyHeaders:
            431
        case HttpError.BodyTooLarge:
            413
        case HttpError.UnsupportedTransferEncoding:
            501
        case HttpError.UnsupportedVersion:
            505
        case _:
            400

def wants_continue(head: &RequestHead) -> bool:
    if head.minor == 0:
        return False
    for field in &head.headers:
        if std.http.same_name(&field.name, "expect") and std.http.same_name(&field.value, "100-continue"):
            return True
    False

pub class Request:
    pub head: RequestHead
    pub target: RequestTarget
    pub body: Bytes
    pub trailers: list[std.http.Header]

pub protocol RequestHandler[E]:
    def handle(self: &mut RequestHandler[E], request: Request, response: &mut Response) -> Result[(), E]:
        pass

class StreamingFactory[F, H, E]:
    pub factory: F

    pub def create(self) -> Result[H, E]:
        self.factory()

class SimpleFactory[F, H, FE, HE]:
    pub factory: F
    pub limits: Limits

    pub def create(self) -> Result[Whole[H, HE], FE | BytesError | AllocError]:
        Ok(Whole[H, HE](self.factory()?, std.bytes.empty()?, std.bytes.empty()?, std.bytes.empty()?, copy(&self.limits)?))

class Whole[H, E]:
    pub handler: H
    pub head: Bytes
    pub body: Bytes
    pub trailers: Bytes
    pub limits: Limits

    pub def receive(self: &mut Whole[H, E], event: Event[i64], response: &mut Response, context: &mut Context[Notice[i64], ServerError]) -> Result[(), E | HttpError | BytesError | AllocError | std.io.StreamError | ServerError]:
        match event:
            case Event.Head(head, _):
                self.head = std.http.encode_request(&head)?
                self.body.clear()
                self.trailers.clear()
            case Event.Body(bytes):
                if bytes.len() > self.limits.max_body - self.body.len():
                    return Err(HttpError.BodyTooLarge)
                self.body.extend(&bytes)?
            case Event.Trailers(fields):
                self.trailers = std.http.encode_response(&ResponseHead(1, 200, "OK", fields))?
            case Event.End:
                saved = replace(self.head, std.bytes.empty()?)
                parse_limits = Limits(saved.len(), saved.len(), self.limits.max_headers, 0)
                mut reader = std.io.buffered_reader(std.io.cursor(saved), 4096)?
                head = std.http.read_request(&mut reader, &parse_limits)?.ok_or(HttpError.Truncated)?
                target = std.http.request_target(&head)?
                body = replace(self.body, std.bytes.empty()?)
                mut trailers: list[std.http.Header] = []?
                if self.trailers.len() > 0:
                    saved_trailers = replace(self.trailers, std.bytes.empty()?)
                    trailer_limits = Limits(saved_trailers.len(), saved_trailers.len(), self.limits.max_headers, 0)
                    mut trailer_reader = std.io.buffered_reader(std.io.cursor(saved_trailers), 4096)?
                    trailer_head = std.http.read_response(&mut trailer_reader, &trailer_limits)?.ok_or(HttpError.Truncated)?
                    trailers = trailer_head.headers
                self.handler.handle(Request(head, target, body, trailers), response)?
                if not response.is_started():
                    response.send_text(500, "Handler sent no response")?
                elif not response.is_done():
                    response.finish()?
            case _:
                pass
        Ok(())

pub def serve[F: Callable[[], Result[H, FE]], H: RequestHandler[HE], FE, HE](listener: TcpListener, factory: F, config: &Config, stop: &CancellationToken) -> Result[Report, ServerError]:
    create = SimpleFactory[F, H, FE, HE](factory, storage(copy(&config.limits))?)
    network(run[SimpleFactory[F, H, FE, HE], Whole[H, HE], i64](listener, create, Nothing, config, stop))

pub def serve_tls[F: Callable[[], Result[H, FE]], H: RequestHandler[HE], FE, HE](listener: TcpListener, tls: ServerConfig, factory: F, config: &Config, stop: &CancellationToken) -> Result[Report, ServerError]:
    create = SimpleFactory[F, H, FE, HE](factory, storage(copy(&config.limits))?)
    network(run[SimpleFactory[F, H, FE, HE], Whole[H, HE], i64](listener, create, Some(tls), config, stop))

pub def serve_events[F: Callable[[], Result[H, FE]], H: Handler[M, HE], M, FE, HE](listener: TcpListener, factory: F, config: &Config, stop: &CancellationToken) -> Result[Report, ServerError]:
    create = StreamingFactory[F, H, FE](factory)
    network(run[StreamingFactory[F, H, FE], H, M](listener, create, Nothing, config, stop))

pub def serve_tls_events[F: Callable[[], Result[H, FE]], H: Handler[M, HE], M, FE, HE](listener: TcpListener, tls: ServerConfig, factory: F, config: &Config, stop: &CancellationToken) -> Result[Report, ServerError]:
    create = StreamingFactory[F, H, FE](factory)
    network(run[StreamingFactory[F, H, FE], H, M](listener, create, Some(tls), config, stop))

def run[F, H, M](listener: TcpListener, factory: F, tls: Option[ServerConfig], config: &Config, stop: &CancellationToken) -> Result[Report, ServerError | AllocError | WaitError | std.actor.StartError | RangeError]:
    if config.capacity < 1 or config.capacity > 1000 or config.heap_limit < 262144 or config.heap_limit > std.actor.max_heap_limit:
        return Err(ServerError.InvalidConfig)
    if config.input_buffer < 64 or config.output_buffer < 64 or config.pending_output < 512 or config.max_requests < 1:
        return Err(ServerError.InvalidConfig)
    if config.limits.max_line < 1 or config.limits.max_head < 1 or config.limits.max_headers < 1 or config.limits.max_body < 0:
        return Err(ServerError.InvalidConfig)
    mut actors = std.actor.stage[Node[F, H], Notice[M], ServerError](config.capacity + 1, 16, 64)?
    actors.add_timers(4 * config.capacity + 8)?
    acceptor = Acceptor(factory=factory, socket=listener, config=copy(config)?, tls=tls, children=Nothing, watch=Nothing, address=Nothing, draining=False, requests=0u64, rejected=0u64, protocol_errors=0u64)
    root = actors.start(Node[F, H](State[F, H].Accepting(acceptor)), 1048576)?
    never = CancellationToken()?
    mut stopping = False
    mut drain_until: Option[Deadline] = Nothing
    mut requests = 0u64
    mut rejected = 0u64
    mut protocol_errors = 0u64
    while True:
        mut budget = milliseconds(100u32)
        match &drain_until:
            case Some(deadline):
                if deadline.expired(&monotonic_now()):
                    break
                remaining = deadline.remaining(&monotonic_now())
                if remaining.as_nanoseconds() < budget.as_nanoseconds():
                    budget = remaining
            case Nothing:
                pass
        until = deadline_after(&monotonic_now(), &budget)?
        ran = match stopping:
            case True:
                actors.run(&until, &never)
            case False:
                actors.run(&until, stop)
        match ran:
            case Ok(_):
                return Err(ServerError.AdmissionStopped)
            case Err(WaitError.TimedOut):
                pass
            case Err(WaitError.Cancelled):
                stopping = True
            case Err(error):
                return Err(error)
        if stopping:
            drop(actors.send(root, Notice[M].Drain))
        mut done = False
        match actors.node(root):
            case Some(node):
                match &node._state:
                    case State.Accepting(acceptor):
                        done = acceptor.done()
                        stopping = stopping or acceptor.draining
                        requests = acceptor.requests
                        rejected = acceptor.rejected
                        protocol_errors = acceptor.protocol_errors
                    case _:
                        pass
            case Nothing:
                return Err(ServerError.AdmissionStopped)
        if stopping and drain_until.is_none():
            drain_until = Some(deadline_after(&monotonic_now(), &config.drain_timeout)?)
        if done:
            break
    # This runs outside all actors and cannot be defeated by full mailboxes,
    # missing timers, or trapping destructors. Drop also handles early errors.
    actors.shutdown()
    Ok(Report(actors.stats(), requests, rejected, protocol_errors))


def application[T, E](result: Result[T, E]) -> Result[T, ServerError]:
    match result:
        case Ok(value):
            Ok(value)
        case Err(_):
            Err(ServerError.Handler)

def server_error(error: AllocError | BytesError | HttpError | NetError | TlsError | TimerError | WaitError | std.actor.StartError | RangeError | ServerError) -> ServerError:
    match error:
        case cause: AllocError:
            ServerError.Allocation(cause)
        case cause: BytesError:
            ServerError.Bytes(cause)
        case cause: HttpError:
            ServerError.Http(cause)
        case cause: NetError:
            ServerError.Net(cause)
        case cause: TlsError:
            ServerError.Tls(cause)
        case cause: TimerError:
            ServerError.Timer(cause)
        case cause: WaitError:
            ServerError.Wait(cause)
        case cause: std.actor.StartError:
            ServerError.Actor(cause)
        case cause: RangeError:
            ServerError.Range(cause)
        case cause: ServerError:
            cause

    Drain
    Resume
    # Reserved for completion credit between admission and connection actors.
    Completed
    CompletedBy(Address)
    Rejected

# Only owned bytes and scalars survive a callback; heads are encoded before
# they enter this queue. Partial writes resume without retaining a borrow.
pub class Response:
    _output: Bytes
    _start: i64
    _limit: i64
    _state: i64
    _remaining: i64
    _head: bool
    _minor: i64
    _keep: bool
    _stopping: bool
    _body_done: bool
    _shutdown: bool

    pub def is_stopping(self) -> bool:
        self._stopping

    pub def close_after(self: &mut Response) -> ():
        self._keep = False

    # Request server shutdown after this response, without a shared token in
    # the connection heap. Admission receives an ordinary copied message.
    pub def shutdown_server(self: &mut Response) -> ():
        self._shutdown = True
        self._keep = False

    pub def is_started(self) -> bool:
        self._state != 0

    pub def is_done(self) -> bool:
        self._state == 4

    pub def pending(self) -> i64:
        self._output.len() - self._start

    pub def space(self) -> i64:
        mut room = self._limit - self.pending() - 64
        if room < 0:
            room = 0
        room

    def begin_response(self: &mut Response, head: ResponseHead, reserve: i64) -> Result[(), HttpError | BytesError | AllocError]:
        if self._state != 0:
            return Err(HttpError.Broken)
        mut owned = head
        if owned.status < 200:
            return Err(HttpError.InvalidStatusLine)
        if std.http.find(&owned.headers, "transfer-encoding").is_some():
            return Err(HttpError.ConflictingFraming)
        if owned.status == 204 and std.http.find(&owned.headers, "content-length").is_some():
            return Err(HttpError.ConflictingFraming)
        # Use HTTP/1.1 persistence here to test the application's close token;
        # request persistence and the emitted version are handled separately.
        owned.minor = 1
        if not std.http.response_keeps_alive(&owned, &Framing.Length(0)):
            self._keep = False
        mut state = 1
        mut length = 0
        match std.http.response_framing(&owned, "GET")?:
            case Framing.Length(size):
                length = size
            case Framing.Empty:
                pass
            case _:
                if self._minor == 1:
                    state = 2
                    owned.add("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")?
                else:
                    state = 3
                    self._keep = False
        owned.minor = self._minor
        if not self._body_done or self._stopping:
            self._keep = False
        if not self._keep:
            owned.add("Connection", "close")?
        elif self._minor == 0:
            owned.add("Connection", "keep-alive")?
        encoded = std.http.encode_response(&owned)?
        if encoded.len() > self._limit - self.pending() - 64:
            return Err(HttpError.HeadTooLarge)
        if reserve > self._limit - self.pending() - 64 - encoded.len():
            return Err(HttpError.BodyTooLarge)
        self.compact()?
        self._output.extend(&encoded)?
        self._state = state
        self._remaining = length
        Ok(())

    # A short result is back-pressure. Keep the remainder and resume on
    # Writable; this never waits for a socket and never exceeds the queue.
    def _write[S: ByteSource](self: &mut Response, source: &S, start: i64, stop: i64) -> Result[i64, HttpError | BytesError]:
        if self._state < 1 or self._state > 3:
            return Err(HttpError.Broken)
        if start < 0 or stop < start or stop > source.len():
            return Err(BytesError.OutOfRange)
        if self._state == 1 and stop - start > self._remaining and not self._head:
            return Err(HttpError.LengthMismatch)
        if self._head:
            return Ok(stop - start)
        mut count = stop - start
        if count > self.space():
            count = self.space()
        if count == 0:
            return Ok(0)
        self.compact()?
        if self._state == 2:
            size = std.http.encode_chunk_size(count)?
            self._output.extend(&size)?
        self._output.extend_range(source, start, start + count)?
        if self._state == 2:
            self._output.extend(b"\r\n")?
        elif self._state == 1:
            self._remaining -= count
        Ok(count)

    def _finish(self: &mut Response) -> Result[(), HttpError | BytesError]:
        if self._state < 1 or self._state > 3:
            return Err(HttpError.Broken)
        if self._state == 1 and self._remaining != 0 and not self._head:
            return Err(HttpError.LengthMismatch)
        if self._state == 2 and not self._head:
            self.compact()?
            self._output.extend(b"0\r\n\r\n")?
        self._state = 4
        Ok(())

    def _respond[S: ByteSource](self: &mut Response, head: ResponseHead, body: &S) -> Result[(), HttpError | BytesError | AllocError]:
        mut owned = head
        if std.http.find(&owned.headers, "content-length").is_some() or std.http.find(&owned.headers, "transfer-encoding").is_some():
            return Err(HttpError.ConflictingFraming)
        if (owned.status == 204 or owned.status == 304) and body.len() != 0:
            return Err(HttpError.LengthMismatch)
        if body.len() > self.space() and not self._head:
            return Err(HttpError.BodyTooLarge)
        if owned.status != 204 and owned.status != 304:
            owned.add("Content-Length", str.from(body.len())?)?
        self.begin_response(owned, 0 if self._head else body.len())?
        if self._write(body, 0, body.len())? != body.len():
            return Err(HttpError.BodyTooLarge)
        self._finish()?
        Ok(())

    def _send[S: ByteSource](self: &mut Response, status: i64, content_type: &str, body: &S) -> Result[(), HttpError | BytesError | AllocError]:
        mut head = std.http.response(status, std.http.server.reason(status))?
        head.add("Content-Type", *content_type)?
        self._respond(head, body)

    def _send_text(self: &mut Response, status: i64, text: &str) -> Result[(), HttpError | BytesError | AllocError]:
        self._send(status, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", &std.bytes.from_text(text)?)

    def compact(self: &mut Response) -> Result[(), BytesError]:
        if self._start > 0:
            self._output.copy_within(self._start, self._output.len(), 0)?
            self._output.truncate(self.pending())?
            self._start = 0
        Ok(())

    pub def start(self: &mut Response, head: ResponseHead) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        network(self.begin_response(head, 0))

    pub def write[S: ByteSource](self: &mut Response, source: &S, start: i64, stop: i64) -> Result[i64, ServerError]:
        network(self._write(source, start, stop))

    pub def finish(self: &mut Response) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        network(self._finish())

    pub def respond[S: ByteSource](self: &mut Response, head: ResponseHead, body: &S) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        network(self._respond(head, body))

    pub def send[S: ByteSource](self: &mut Response, status: i64, content_type: &str, body: &S) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        network(self._send(status, content_type, body))

    pub def send_text(self: &mut Response, status: i64, text: &str) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        network(self._send_text(status, text))

# The same driver uses TCP or TLS. Both transports advance only on available
# bytes and return back-pressure rather than waiting.
enum Wire:
    Plain(Connection)
    Secure(TlsConnection)

    pub def input(self) -> &Bytes:
        match self:
            case Wire.Plain(connection):
                connection.input()
            case Wire.Secure(connection):
                connection.input()

    pub def input_start(self) -> i64:

class Acceptor[F]:
    socket: TcpListener
    factory: F
    config: Config
    tls: Option[ServerConfig]
    children: Option[list[Address]]
    watch: Option[Watch]
    address: Option[Address]
    draining: bool
    requests: u64
    rejected: u64
    protocol_errors: u64
    # A child cannot submit its next completion until this credit is returned,
    # so at most one address per admitted child is retained here.
    acknowledgements: Option[list[Address]]
    resuming: bool

    def flush_acknowledgements[M](self: &mut Acceptor[F], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> ():
        match &mut self.acknowledgements:
            case Some(pending):
                mut index = 0
                while index < len(pending):
                    match context.send(pending[index], Notice[M].Completed):
                        case Ok(_):
                            pass
                        case Err(std.actor.Undelivered.Full(_)):
                            index += 1
                            continue
                        case Err(std.actor.Undelivered.Gone(_)):
                            pass
                    last = pending.pop().unwrap()
                    if index < len(pending):
                        pending[index] = last
                if len(pending) > 0 and not self.resuming:
                    match context.send(context.address(), Notice[M].Resume):
                        case Ok(_):
                            self.resuming = True
                        case Err(_):
                            pass
            case Nothing:
                pass

    def receive[M](self: &mut Acceptor[F], mail: Mail[Notice[M], ServerError], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match mail:
            case Mail.Ready(watch, _):
                if not self.draining and self.watch.unwrap().key() == watch.key():
                    match &mut self.children:
                        case Some(children):
                            if len(children) < self.config.capacity:
                                match context.spawn_isolated(0, self.config.heap_limit):
                                    case Ok(child):
                                        storage(children.append(child))?
                                        return Ok(())
                                    case Err(_):
                                        pass
                        case Nothing:
                            pass
                    # Refusing never blocks or constructs TLS state.
                    drop(self.socket.accept_now())
                    self.rejected += 1u64
            case Mail.Down(child, _, _):
                match &mut self.children:
                    case Some(children):
                        for index in range(len(children)):
                            if children[index].key() == child.key():
                                last = children.pop().unwrap()
                                if index < len(children):
                                    children[index] = last
                                break
                    case Nothing:
                        pass
            case Mail.Message(Notice.Completed):
                self.requests += 1u64
            case Mail.Message(Notice.CompletedBy(child)):
                self.requests += 1u64
                match &mut self.acknowledgements:
                    case Some(pending):
                        storage(pending.append(child))?
                    case Nothing:
                        pass
            case Mail.Message(Notice.Resume):
                self.resuming = False
            case Mail.Message(Notice.Rejected):
                self.protocol_errors += 1u64
            case Mail.Message(Notice.Drain):
                if not self.draining:
                    self.draining = True
                    drop(context.unwatch(&self.socket))
                    drop(self.socket.close())
                # Retrying Drain is intentional: bounded child mailboxes may
                # have been full during an earlier notification.
                match &self.children:
                    case Some(children):
                        for child in children:
                            drop(context.send(*child, Notice[M].Drain))
                    case Nothing:
                        pass
            case _:
                pass
        self.flush_acknowledgements(context)
        Ok(())

    def done(self) -> bool:
        if not self.draining:
            return False
        match &self.children:
            case Some(children):
                len(children) == 0
            case Nothing:
                True

class Client[F, H]:
    socket: Option[TcpStream]
    factory: F
    config: Config
    session: Option[Session]
    parent: Address
    handler: Option[H]
    wire: Option[Wire]
    decoder: Option[Decoder]
    response: Option[Response]
    requests: i64
    phase: i64
    timer: Option[Timer]
    draining: bool
    lingering: i64
    reported: bool
    resuming: bool
    completing: bool
    shutdown_pending: bool
    retiring: bool
    failure: Option[ServerError]
    retry: Option[Timer]
    awaiting: bool


    def set_deadline[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match replace(self.timer, Nothing):
            case Some(timer):
                drop(context.cancel(timer))
            case Nothing:
                pass
        span = match self.phase:
            case 0:
                nanoseconds(self.config.handshake_timeout.as_nanoseconds())
            case 1:
                nanoseconds(self.config.idle_timeout.as_nanoseconds())
            case 2:
                nanoseconds(self.config.head_timeout.as_nanoseconds())
            case 3:
                nanoseconds(self.config.body_timeout.as_nanoseconds())
            case 5:
                seconds(2u32)
            case _:
                nanoseconds(self.config.response_timeout.as_nanoseconds())
        if span.as_nanoseconds() > 0u64:
            self.timer = Some(network(context.after(&span, -1))?)
        Ok(())

    def resume[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        if not self.resuming and self.retry.is_none() and not self.awaiting:
            # A bounded continuation yields without a timer. A full mailbox
            # already makes this actor runnable, so it needs no extra wakeup.
            match context.send(context.address(), Notice[M].Resume):
                case Ok(_):
                    self.resuming = True
                case Err(_):
                    pass
        Ok(())

    def has_control(self) -> bool:
        self.shutdown_pending or self.completing or self.awaiting

    def flush_control[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> ():
        if self.retry.is_some():
            return
        if self.shutdown_pending:
            match context.send(self.parent, Notice[M].Drain):
                case Ok(_):
                    self.shutdown_pending = False
                case Err(_):
                    pass
        if self.completing:
            # One accepted notification per connection remains outstanding.
            # Waiting for its acknowledgement prevents fast connections from
            # continually taking the acceptor slots that others need.
            match context.send(self.parent, Notice[M].CompletedBy(context.address())):
                case Ok(_):
                    self.completing = False
                    self.awaiting = True
                case Err(_):
                    pass
        if self.shutdown_pending or self.completing:
            # The acceptor handles one message per scheduling round. Spinning
            # all blocked children every round only refills the same mailbox.
            # A private timer lets it drain; live application mail still runs.
            match context.after(&milliseconds(1u32), -2):
                case Ok(timer):
                    self.retry = Some(timer)
                case Err(_):
                    # Application timers share this bounded pool. Preserve
                    # control delivery even when none is available.
                    drop(self.resume(context))

    def stop[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        self.retiring = True
        if self.has_control():
            self.resume(context)?
        else:
            context.stop()
        Ok(())

    def receive[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], mail: Mail[Notice[M], ServerError], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match &mail:
            case Mail.Message(Notice.Resume):
                self.resuming = False
            case Mail.Message(Notice.Completed):
                if self.awaiting:
                    self.awaiting = False
                    self.reported = True
            case _:
                pass
        match &mail:
            case Mail.Timer(timer):
                match self.retry:
                    case Some(retry):
                        if retry.key() == timer.key():
                            self.retry = Nothing
                    case Nothing:
                        pass
            case _:
                pass
        self.flush_control(context)
        if self.retiring:
            # The connection has already ended. Keep only its bounded control
            # notifications alive; application mail no longer has a recipient.
            if self.has_control():
                self.resume(context)?
                return Ok(())
            match replace(self.failure, Nothing):
                case Some(error):
                    return Err(error)
                case Nothing:
                    context.stop()
                    return Ok(())
        # A full parent mailbox never discards live application messages or
        # one-shot timers. Only final retirement waits for control delivery.
        match self.drive(mail, context):
            case Ok(_):
                Ok(())
            case Err(error):
                if not self.has_control():
                    return Err(error)
                self.retiring = True
                self.failure = Some(error)
                self.resume(context)?
                Ok(())

    def drive[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], mail: Mail[Notice[M], ServerError], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        mut wire = replace(self.wire, Nothing).unwrap()
        mut decoder = replace(self.decoder, Nothing).unwrap()
        mut reply = replace(self.response, Nothing).unwrap()
        mut handler = replace(self.handler, Nothing).unwrap()
        events = wire.handle(&mail, context)?
        if events.expired.is_some():
            wire.close(context)?
            self.stop(context)?
        else:
            match mail:
                case Mail.Timer(timer):
                    match &self.timer:
                        case Some(phase_timer):
                            if timer.key() == phase_timer.key():
                                if self.phase == 2 or self.phase == 3:
                                    self.refuse(&mut reply, 408)?
                                    self.phase = 4
                                    self.set_deadline(context)?
                                else:
                                    wire.close(context)?
                                    self.stop(context)?
                                    return Ok(())
                        case Nothing:
                            pass
                    if timer.tag() >= 0 and not events.mine:
                        self.call(&mut handler, Event[M].Actor(Mail[Notice[M], ServerError].Timer(timer)), &mut reply, context)?
                case Mail.Message(Notice.Resume):
                    self.resuming = False
                case Mail.Message(Notice.Completed):
                    pass
                case Mail.Message(Notice.Message(message)):
                    self.call(&mut handler, Event[M].Message(message), &mut reply, context)?
                case Mail.Message(Notice.Drain):
                    if not self.draining:
                        self.draining = True
                        reply._stopping = True
                        reply._keep = False
                        if self.phase <= 1:
                            self.close_after_flush(&mut wire, context)?
                        else:
                            self.call(&mut handler, Event[M].Stopping, &mut reply, context)?
                case Mail.Ready(watch, ready):
                    if not events.mine:
                        self.call(&mut handler, Event[M].Actor(Mail[Notice[M], ServerError].Ready(watch, ready)), &mut reply, context)?
                case Mail.Stop:
                    drop(wire.close(context))
                    return Ok(())
                case _ as other:
                    self.call(&mut handler, Event[M].Actor(other), &mut reply, context)?
            if not self.retiring:
                self.advance(&mut wire, &mut decoder, &mut reply, &mut handler, context)?
        self.wire = Some(wire)
        self.decoder = Some(decoder)
        self.response = Some(reply)
        self.handler = Some(handler)
        Ok(())

    def call[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], handler: &mut H, event: Event[M], reply: &mut Response, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        outcome = handler.receive(event, reply, context)
        if reply._shutdown:
            self.shutdown_pending = True
            reply._shutdown = False
        self.flush_control(context)
        match outcome:
            case Ok(_):
                pass
            case Err(_):
                if reply.is_started():
                    return Err(ServerError.Handler)
                self.refuse(reply, 500)?
        Ok(())

    def refuse(self: &mut Client[F, H], reply: &mut Response, status: i64) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        if reply.is_started():
            return Err(ServerError.Http(HttpError.Broken))
        reply._keep = False
        reply._body_done = True
        network(reply.send_text(status, std.http.server.reason(status)))?
        self.phase = 4
        Ok(())

    def close_after_flush[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], wire: &mut Wire, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        wire.shutdown_write(context)?
        self.phase = 5
        self.set_deadline(context)?
        if not wire.reading() and wire.pending() == 0:
            self.stop(context)?
        else:
            self.resume(context)?
        Ok(())

    def advance[M](self: &mut Client[F, H], wire: &mut Wire, decoder: &mut Decoder, reply: &mut Response, handler: &mut H, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        if self.shutdown_pending:
            self.resume(context)?
            return Ok(())
        if self.phase == 0:
            if not wire.established():
                return Ok(())
            self.phase = 1
            self.set_deadline(context)?
        if self.phase == 5:
            count = wire.available()
            self.lingering += count
            wire.consume(count, context)?
            if (not wire.reading() or self.lingering >= 16777216) and wire.pending() == 0:
                wire.close(context)?
                self.stop(context)?
            elif wire.available() > 0:
                self.resume(context)?
            return Ok(())
        if self.phase == 1 and wire.available() > 0:
            self.phase = 2
            self.set_deadline(context)?
        # Bounded decoder events per actor turn. A continuation timer handles
        # input already buffered when no further socket readiness is needed.
        mut progress = False
        for _ in range(16):
            if self.phase != 2 and self.phase != 3:
                break
            if reply.is_started() and not reply.is_done() and reply.space() == 0:
                break
            next = decoder.feed(wire.input(), wire.input_start(), wire.input_stop())
            match next:
                case Err(error):
                    drop(context.send(self.parent, Notice[M].Rejected))
                    self.refuse(reply, error_status(&error))?
                    self.phase = 4
                    self.set_deadline(context)?
                    break
                case Ok(pair):
                    consumed, event = pair
                    wire.consume(consumed, context)?
                    progress = consumed > 0
                    match event:
                        case Some(std.http.decoder.Event.Head(head, target, framing)):
                            self.requests += 1
                            reply._head = head.method == "HEAD"
                            reply._minor = head.minor
                            reply._keep = not self.draining and self.requests < self.config.max_requests and std.http.request_keeps_alive(&head)
                            expect = wants_continue(&head)
                            self.phase = 3
                            self.set_deadline(context)?
                            self.call(handler, Event[M].Head(head, target), reply, context)?
                            if expect and not reply.is_started():
                                match framing:
                                    case Framing.Length(0) | Framing.Empty:
                                        pass
                                    case _:
                                        storage(reply._output.extend(b"HTTP/1.1 100 Continue\r\n\r\n"))?
                            progress = True
                        case Some(std.http.decoder.Event.Body(bytes)):
                            self.call(handler, Event[M].Body(bytes), reply, context)?
                            progress = True
                        case Some(std.http.decoder.Event.Trailers(fields)):
                            self.call(handler, Event[M].Trailers(fields), reply, context)?
                            progress = True
                        case Some(std.http.decoder.Event.End):
                            reply._body_done = True
                            self.phase = 4
                            self.set_deadline(context)?
                            self.call(handler, Event[M].End, reply, context)?
                            progress = True
                        case Nothing:
                            pass
                    if reply.is_done() and not reply._body_done:
                        reply._keep = False
                        self.phase = 4
                        self.set_deadline(context)?
                    if not progress:
                        break
        if not wire.reading() and wire.available() == 0 and not progress and (self.phase == 2 or self.phase == 3):
            match decoder.finish():
                case Err(error):
                    self.refuse(reply, error_status(&error))?
                    self.phase = 4
                case Ok(_):
                    self.close_after_flush(wire, context)?
                    return Ok(())
        if self.phase == 1 and not wire.reading():
            self.close_after_flush(wire, context)?
            return Ok(())
        if self.shutdown_pending:
            self.resume(context)?
            return Ok(())
        before = reply.pending()
        if before > 0:
            mut stop = reply._output.len()
            if stop - reply._start > 16384:
                stop = reply._start + 16384
            count = wire.write(&reply._output, reply._start, stop, context)?
            reply._start += count
            if reply._start == reply._output.len():
                reply._output.clear()
                reply._start = 0
            if count > 0 and not reply.is_done() and reply.is_started():
                self.call(handler, Event[M].Writable, reply, context)?
        if self.shutdown_pending:
            self.resume(context)?
            return Ok(())
        if reply.is_done() and reply.pending() == 0 and wire.pending() == 0:
            if not self.reported:
                if not self.completing and not self.awaiting:
                    self.completing = True
                    self.flush_control(context)
                if not self.reported:
                    return Ok(())
            if not reply._keep or self.draining:
                self.close_after_flush(wire, context)?
                return Ok(())
            network(decoder.reset())?
            reply._state = 0
            reply._remaining = 0
            reply._body_done = False
            self.reported = False
            self.phase = 1
            self.set_deadline(context)?
            # EOF may have arrived while the completion awaited its credit;
            # there is then no further readiness to close the idle connection.
            progress = wire.available() > 0 or not wire.reading()
        if progress or (reply.pending() > 0 and wire.pending() == 0):
            self.resume(context)?
        Ok(())

# phase 0 handshake, 1 idle, 2 head, 3 body, 4 response, 5 lingering.
# Only one request is decoded at a time; pipelined input remains in the
# bounded transport buffer until its preceding response has drained.
enum State[F, H]:
    Accepting(Acceptor[F])
    Serving(Client[F, H])

# Public for cross-module generic Stage dispatch; construction stays private.
pub class Node[F, H]:
    _state: State[F, H]

    pub def started[M](self: &mut Node[F, H], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match &mut self._state:
            case State.Accepting(acceptor):
                acceptor.address = Some(context.address())
                acceptor.children = Some(storage(list[Address].with_capacity(acceptor.config.capacity))?)
                acceptor.acknowledgements = Some(storage(list[Address].with_capacity(acceptor.config.capacity))?)
                acceptor.watch = Some(network(context.watch(&acceptor.socket, Interest.Read))?)
            case State.Serving(client):
                mut socket = match replace(client.socket, Nothing):
                    case Some(stream):
                        stream
                    case Nothing:
                        context.stop()
                        return Ok(())
                drop(socket.set_no_delay(True))
                limits = std.actor.net.Limits(client.config.input_buffer, client.config.output_buffer, seconds(0u32), nanoseconds(client.config.write_timeout.as_nanoseconds()))
                net = network(std.actor.net.connection(socket, &limits))?
                mut wire = match replace(client.session, Nothing):
                    case Some(session):
                        Wire.Secure(network(std.actor.tls.over(net, session, client.config.input_buffer))?)
                    case Nothing:
                        Wire.Plain(net)
                wire.start(context)?
                client.phase = 0 if not wire.established() else 1
                client.wire = Some(wire)
                client.handler = Some(application(client.factory.create())?)
                client.decoder = Some(storage(std.http.decoder.decoder(&client.config.limits))?)
                client.response = Some(storage(response(client.config.pending_output))?)
                client.set_deadline(context)?
        Ok(())

    pub def receive[M](self: &mut Node[F, H], mail: Mail[Notice[M], ServerError], context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[(), ServerError]:
        match &mut self._state:
            case State.Accepting(acceptor):
                acceptor.receive(mail, context)
            case State.Serving(client):
                client.receive(mail, context)

    pub def spawn[M](self, tag: i64, child: Address, context: &mut Context[Notice[M], ServerError]) -> Result[Option[Node[F, H]], ServerError]:
        match &self._state:
            case State.Accepting(acceptor):
                stream: Option[TcpStream] = match acceptor.socket.accept_now():
                    case Ok(socket):
                        Some(socket)
                    case Err(_):
                        Nothing
                session: Option[Session] = match &acceptor.tls:
                    case Some(tls):
                        Some(network(server_session(tls))?)
                    case Nothing:
                        Nothing
                # TLS configs cannot be copied. The session is constructed in
                # the child heap under isolated admission; any failure retires
                # this child. User factory and socket buffers run in started.
                Ok(Some(Node[F, H](State[F, H].Serving(Client[F, H](stream, storage(copy(&acceptor.factory))?, storage(copy(&acceptor.config))?, session, acceptor.address.unwrap(), Nothing, Nothing, Nothing, Nothing, 0, 1, Nothing, False, 0, False, False, False, False, False, Nothing, Nothing, False)))))
            case State.Serving(_):
                Ok(Nothing)

def error_status(error: &HttpError) -> i64:
    match error:
        case HttpError.LineTooLong | HttpError.HeadTooLarge | HttpError.TooManyHeaders:
            431
        case HttpError.BodyTooLarge:
            413
        case HttpError.UnsupportedTransferEncoding:
            501
        case HttpError.UnsupportedVersion:
            505
        case _:
            400

def wants_continue(head: &RequestHead) -> bool:
    if head.minor == 0:
        return False
    for field in &head.headers:
        if std.http.same_name(&field.name, "expect") and std.http.same_name(&field.value, "100-continue"):
            return True
    False
